AxisConst.description:
Constant axis with a fixed value.

A constant axis represents a dimension that has a fixed, compile-time known value.
This is useful for dimensions that don't vary across different instances of the
same kernel definition, such as embedding dimensions or hidden layer sizes.

type.description: The type identifier for constant axes.
type.title: Type

value.description: The constant integer value of this axis dimension.
value.title: Value

description.description: An optional human-readable description explaining the purpose of this axis.
description.title: Description

AxisConst.title: AxisConst

AxisVar.description:
Variable axis that can be specified at runtime.

A variable axis represents a dimension whose value is determined at runtime
based on the actual input data. Its value will be bound to the input tensor
dimension at runtime.
AxisVar.title: AxisVar

DType.description:
Supported data types for tensors.

Enumeration of all data types that can be used in tensor specifications.
Includes both floating-point and integer types commonly used in machine
learning and high-performance computing applications.
DType.title: DType

TensorSpec.description:
Specification for a tensor including shape and data type, to use as input or output of a
kernel.

This includes the symbolic shape (referencing defined axes) and the data type.
Scalars are represented with a None shape.

shape.description: List of axis names defining the tensor shape. None for scalar values.
shape.title: Shape

dtype.description: The data type of all elements in this tensor.

description.description: An optional human-readable description of this tensor's purpose and usage.
description.title: Description

TensorSpec.title: TensorSpec

Definition.description:
Complete definition of a computational workload.

A Definition provides a formal, machine-readable specification for a computational
workload. It defines the tensor formats, dimension semantics, and computational
logic through a reference implementation. This serves as the single source of
truth for kernel development and optimization.

name.description: A unique, human-readable name for the kernel definition.
name.title: Name

axes.description:
Dictionary of symbolic dimensions used in tensor shapes. The axes will be bound to the
input tensor dimensions at runtime.
axes.title: Axes

inputs.description:
Named input tensors required by this kernel. The order of inputs is preserved as the
kernel's interface.
inputs.title: Inputs

outputs.description:
Named output tensors produced by this kernel. The names of the output must not overlap
with the names of the inputs. The order of outputs is preserved as the kernel's interface.
outputs.title: Outputs

reference.description:
Reference implementation code. It defines the compute logic of the kernel. Must be a valid
Python code with a 'run' function that takes the input tensors and returns the output tensors.
reference.title: Reference

tags.description:
Optional list of tags for grouping and filtering kernels. It's used in the FlashInfer-Bench
website.
tags.title: Tags

description.description: Optional human-readable description of the kernel's purpose.
description.title: Description

constraints.description: Optional list of constraint expressions describing relationships between axes.
constraints.title: Constraints

Definition.title: Definition

Correctness.description:
Correctness metrics from numerical evaluation.

Contains error measurements comparing the solution output against
a reference implementation to assess numerical accuracy.

max_relative_error.description: Maximum relative error observed across all output elements.
max_relative_error.title: Max Relative Error

max_absolute_error.description: Maximum absolute error observed across all output elements.
max_absolute_error.title: Max Absolute Error

Correctness.title: Correctness

Environment.description:
Environment information from evaluation execution.

Records the hardware and software environment details from when
the evaluation was performed, enabling reproducibility analysis.

hardware.description: Hardware identifier where the evaluation was performed (e.g., 'NVIDIA_H100').
hardware.title: Hardware

libs.description: Dictionary of library names to version strings used during evaluation.
libs.title: Libs

Environment.title: Environment

Evaluation.description:
Complete evaluation result for a solution on a workload.

Records the full outcome of benchmarking a solution implementation
against a specific workload, including status, metrics, and environment.

status.description: The overall evaluation status indicating success or failure mode.

environment.description: Environment details where the evaluation was performed.

timestamp.description: Timestamp when the evaluation was performed (ISO format recommended).
timestamp.title: Timestamp

log.description: Captured stdout/stderr from the evaluation run.
log.title: Log

correctness.description: Correctness metrics (present for PASSED and INCORRECT_NUMERICAL status).

performance.description: Performance metrics (present only for PASSED status).

Evaluation.title: Evaluation

EvaluationStatus.description:
Status codes for evaluation results.

Enumeration of all possible outcomes when evaluating a solution
against a workload, covering success and various failure modes.
EvaluationStatus.title: EvaluationStatus

Performance.description:
Performance metrics from timing evaluation.

Contains timing measurements and performance comparisons from
benchmarking the solution against reference implementations.

reference_latency_ms.description: Reference implementation latency in milliseconds for comparison.
reference_latency_ms.title: Reference Latency Ms

speedup_factor.description: Performance speedup factor compared to reference (reference_time / solution_time).
speedup_factor.title: Speedup Factor

Performance.title: Performance

RandomInput.description:
Random input generation descriptor.

Represents a specification for generating random tensor input data
during workload execution and benchmarking.

type.description: The input type identifier for random data generation.
type.title: Type

RandomInput.title: RandomInput

SafetensorsInput.description:
Input specification for data loaded from safetensors files.

Represents tensor data that will be loaded from a safetensors file
using a specific tensor key within that file.

type.description: The input type identifier for safetensors data.
type.title: Type

path.description:
Path to the safetensors file containing the tensor data. The path is relative to the root
path of the TraceSet.
path.title: Path

tensor_key.description: Key identifier for the specific tensor within the safetensors file.
tensor_key.title: Tensor Key

SafetensorsInput.title: SafetensorsInput

ScalarInput.description:
Scalar literal input specification.

Represents a scalar value (integer, float, or boolean) that will be
used as a direct input parameter to the computational workload.

type.description: The input type identifier for scalar values.
type.title: Type

value.description: The scalar value to be used as input. Must be int, float, or bool.
value.title: Value

ScalarInput.title: ScalarInput

Workload.description:
Concrete workload configuration for benchmarking.

Defines a specific instance of a computational workload with concrete
values for all variable axes and specifications for all input data.
This represents an executable configuration that can be benchmarked.

axes.description:
Dictionary mapping axis names to their concrete integer values. All values must be
positive.
axes.title: Axes

inputs.description: Dictionary mapping input names to their data specifications.
inputs.title: Inputs

uuid.description: Unique identifier for this specific workload configuration.
uuid.title: Uuid

Workload.title: Workload

Trace.description:
Complete trace linking a solution to a definition with evaluation results.

A Trace represents the complete record of benchmarking a specific solution
implementation against a specific computational workload definition. It includes
the workload configuration and evaluation results.

Special case: A "workload trace" contains only definition and workload fields
(with solution and evaluation set to None), representing a workload configuration
without an actual benchmark execution.

definition.description: Name of the Definition that specifies the computational workload.
definition.title: Definition

workload.description: Concrete workload configuration with specific axis values and inputs.

solution.description: Name of the Solution implementation (None for workload-only traces).
solution.title: Solution

evaluation.description: Evaluation results from benchmarking (None for workload-only traces).

Trace.title: Trace

BuildSpec.description:
Build specification for a solution implementation.

Contains all technical specifications required to build and execute a solution, including
language, hardware targets, dependencies, entry point, and build commands.

target_hardware.description:
List of hardware this solution is compatible with. E.g. 'cpu', 'cuda'. Note this is not used
in verification and building now.
target_hardware.title: Target Hardware

entry_point.description:
The exact path to the function to be called. Format: '{file_path}::{function_name}'
(e.g., 'main.py::run').
entry_point.title: Entry Point

dependencies.description:
Optional list of required libraries or packages. E.g. for CUDA, we support 'cublas',
'cudnn', 'cutlass'
dependencies.title: Dependencies

destination_passing_style.description:
Whether to use destination passing style for the solution. If True, the solution should
accept the output tensors as the last arguments. If False, the solution should return the
output tensors.
destination_passing_style.title: Destination Passing Style

binding.description:
The binding type to use for C++/CUDA solutions. If None, defaults to 'tvm-ffi' for
C++/CUDA languages. Ignored for Python and Triton languages.

BuildSpec.title: BuildSpec

SourceFile.description:
A single source code file in a solution implementation.

Represents a source code file with its relative path and complete content.
The file content is validated for syntax correctness based on the file extension.

path.description:
The relative path of the file, including its name and extension (e.g., 'src/kernel.cu',
'main.py'). When compiling the solution, a temporary solution source directory will be
created, and the file will be placed according to this path. The path should not contain
parent directory traversal ("..").
path.title: Path

content.description: The complete text content of the source file.
content.title: Content

SourceFile.title: SourceFile

SupportedBindings.description:
Supported bindings for C++/CUDA solution implementations.

Enumeration of binding types that can be used to interface compiled
C++/CUDA code with Python.
SupportedBindings.title: SupportedBindings

SupportedLanguages.description:
Supported programming languages for solution implementations.

Enumeration of programming languages that can be used to implement
solutions for computational workloads.
SupportedLanguages.title: SupportedLanguages

Solution.description:
A concrete implementation for a given Definition.

Represents a complete solution that provides a high-performance implementation
for a computational workload defined by a Definition. Contains all source code,
build specifications, and metadata required for building, interfacing, and
benchmarking the implementation.

name.description: A unique, human-readable name for this specific solution (e.g., 'rmsnorm_triton_v1_h100').
name.title: Name

definition.description: The name of the Definition this implementation solves.
definition.title: Definition

author.description: The name of the author or agent system that created this solution.
author.title: Author

spec.description: Technical specifications for building and executing this solution.

sources.description: Array of source code files representing the complete implementation.
sources.title: Sources

description.description: Optional human-readable description of the solution's technique or approach.
description.title: Description

Solution.title: Solution

EvalConfig.description: Per-definition eval parameters. All fields Optional; None means inherit from parent layer.
EvalConfig.title: EvalConfig

BenchmarkConfig.description:
Configuration for benchmark runs. Mirrors the YAML structure exactly.

All fields have default values to make configuration optional.
BenchmarkConfig.title: BenchmarkConfig
